content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, fire is primarily a symbol of God's presence and holiness, which manifests in two closely linked ways: divine judgment upon sin and purifying refinement of God's people. The dominant summary formula is that fire represents the holy presence of God that both consumes what is evil and purifies what is to be preserved ('our God is a consuming fire').", "primary_basis": ["Exodus 3:2 (God appears to Moses in the burning bush)", "Exodus 13:21-22 (pillar of fire signifying God's guiding presence)", "Exodus 19:18 (the LORD descends on Sinai in fire)", "Deuteronomy 4:24 (the LORD your God is a consuming fire)", "Hebrews 12:29 (our God is a consuming fire)", "Malachi 3:2-3 (the refiner's fire purifying the sons of Levi)", "Zechariah 13:9 (refining a remnant as silver and gold are refined)", "1 Corinthians 3:13-15 (fire testing the quality of each one's work)", "1 Peter 1:7 (faith tested by fire like gold)", "Isaiah 6:6-7 (burning coal purging Isaiah's lips)", "Matthew 3:11-12 / Luke 3:16-17 (baptism with the Holy Spirit and fire; burning of chaff)", "Leviticus 9:24 / 1 Kings 18:38 (fire from heaven consuming the sacrifice as divine acceptance and judgment)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Fire as the Holy Spirit, especially the Spirit's empowering presence at Pentecost (tongues of fire), and by extension spiritual fervor and empowerment.", "basis": ["Acts 2:3-4", "Matthew 3:11 / Luke 3:16 (baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire)", "1 Thessalonians 5:19 (do not quench the Spirit)", "2 Timothy 1:6 (fan into flame the gift of God)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Fire as eternal punishment or hell (final destructive judgment on the wicked), often treated as a distinct eschatological usage rather than a purifying one.", "basis": ["Matthew 25:41 (eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels)", "Mark 9:43-48 (unquenchable fire; Gehenna)", "Revelation 20:14-15 (lake of fire)", "2 Thessalonians 1:7-8", "Jude 7 (Sodom as an example of eternal fire)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Fire as trial, testing, and affliction that believers pass through, a metaphor for suffering that proves and strengthens faith.", "basis": ["1 Peter 1:7", "1 Peter 4:12 (fiery trial)", "Isaiah 43:2 (when you walk through the fire you shall not be burned)", "Daniel 3 (the fiery furnace)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Fire as the word of God, powerful, penetrating, and irrepressible.", "basis": ["Jeremiah 23:29 (is not my word like fire?)", "Jeremiah 20:9 (a fire shut up in my bones)", "Luke 24:32 (did not our hearts burn within us?)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Fire as unruly or destructive human passion, especially the tongue, anger, lust, or strife.", "basis": ["James 3:5-6 (the tongue is a fire)", "Proverbs 6:27-28 (can a man carry fire in his bosom?)", "Proverbs 26:20-21 (strife kindled like fire)", "1 Corinthians 7:9 (better to marry than to burn)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Fire as purgatorial purification after death (a distinctly Roman Catholic reading of the testing fire).", "basis": ["1 Corinthians 3:13-15 as interpreted in Catholic tradition regarding purgatory"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "Fire is one of the most heavily used and well-catalogued symbols in Scripture, and reference works (e.g., dictionaries of biblical imagery, standard commentaries) show broad agreement on its core meaning: the manifest presence and holiness of God, expressed as judgment on evil and purification of the faithful. The main interpretive variation is not disagreement over this core but over which sub-sense governs a given passage (e.g., whether 'baptism with fire' in Matthew 3:11 refers to Pentecost, purification, or judgment is a well-known exegetical debate). Context determines which strand applies; no single sub-meaning covers every occurrence, but the judgment/purification/divine-presence cluster is the recognizable consensus."}
